title: Jingchen Zhu (朱景琛)
text:
Welcome to my academic website.
My research lies at the intersection of organizational economics, behavioral economics, and political economy. I combine proprietary within-firm data, field experiments, and surveys to study digital transformation and AI adoption, particularly among firms in developing countries. I examine how digital and AI-enabled technologies affect firm performance and organizational outcomes, how they interact with traditional management practices, and what barriers firms face in adopting and effectively using them.
A central part of my research is conducted in collaboration with firms across a range of industries. In a large manufacturing company, I studied how the digitalization of production processes and managerial task allocation can improve talent retention by reducing employee burnout. I also conducted a field experiment at a construction company to examine how giving workers greater voice affects conformity. My current work with a large livestock company investigates how the introduction of AI into production processes shapes organizational attention and responsiveness.
A new strand of my research extends this firm-centered approach to questions in international trade and political economy. I have recently started some new projects studying how firms adapt their international operations and market strategies to an increasingly fragmented global environment.
